verdict.rationale: Godot is governed by a nonprofit foundation and released under the permissive MIT license, which is irrevocable and applies uniformly to all past and future versions — there's no mechanism (unlike Unity's per-install fee controversy) for retroactive repricing of shipped games, and docs explicitly state you're free to use it for any purpose and license your own games as you see fit. Community commentary corroborates Godot's free/open positioning as a contrast to engines with royalty or fee surprises. Missing for 10: no explicit third-party legal analysis or historical case study confirming license terms have never been retroactively altered across major version bumps.
